title: Declining force of selection with age

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Declining force of selection with age

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The strength of selection on survival falls with age after reproduction begins, so senescence is an inevitable outcome of natural selection.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: s(a) = \frac{\partial r}{\partial \ln p_a} = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{x=a+1}^{\infty} e^{-rx} l_x m_x, non-increasing in a

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The moulding of senescence by natural selection

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: The moulding of senescence by natural selection (1966)

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: W. D. Hamilton (1966) The moulding of senescence by natural selection

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: an age-structured population with fixed age-specific fertility and no growth or repair after maturity

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: the formula for s(a) is proved. The inevitability claim is refuted as stated: Jones et al. (2013) found species with flat or declining mortality with age, consistent with life histories where fertility rises with size.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: s(a) = \frac{\partial r}{\partial \ln p_a} = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{x=a+1}^{\infty} e^{-rx} l_x m_x, non-increasing in a

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: Compare age trajectories of mortality and fertility across many species with the trajectories that s(a) predicts from each species' own life table.
